clips.text_zh: 黃金依家咁高，金礦股好難揀。70/30定80/20 gold/silver好？定係80%金期貨+20%金礦股穩陣啲？我個倉小，唔想all in一邊
clips.text_en_b1: Ok anon, help me out. Should I go 80% gold futures and 20% gold miners? Or 80% gold and 20% silver? Right now gold is at record highs and I do not want to be all-in on one side. My account is small so I need to keep it simple. Which split is safer this quarter?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon debating gold vs silver allocation

signal.rationale: Anon is asking how to allocate into gold right now, the implied direction is long gold but undecided on mix

clips.text_en_b2: Alright anon, I could use some advice here. With gold hovering near record highs, I am torn between going 80% gold futures paired with 20% gold miners, or splitting 70/30 or 80/20 between physical gold and silver instead. My account is fairly small, so I would rather not go all-in on a single bet. Which allocation actually holds up better this quarter, given how stretched valuations look?
clips.text_en_c1: With gold trading at unprecedented levels, identifying exposure in miners has become considerably more difficult. I am weighing three configurations: a 70/30 gold-to-silver split, an 80/20 variant, or a blend of 80 percent gold futures against 20 percent mining equities, which ought to provide marginally greater stability. Given that my position size is modest, concentrating capital in a single asset class is the last thing I want to do. What allocation would you consider prudent for the current quarter, assuming continued macro uncertainty and a potential rotation once bullion peaks?
clips.text_en_c2: Given gold's present vertiginous ascent, selecting the appropriate vehicle within the broader precious-metals complex becomes a genuinely vexing exercise. The question of whether to favour an 80/20 gold-to-silver allocation, or alternatively to divide the position between gold futures and equity exposure via gold producers, is, in essence, a question of correlational risk and capital efficiency. With bullion at historic highs and one's account conspicuously modest, the imperative to avoid unilateral concentration grows correspondingly acute. A hybrid approach—predominantly futures, with a marginal allocation to mining equities—might furnish superior liquidity, although the inherent volatility of producer shares remains a non-trivial consideration this cycle.

clips.text_zh: lol 4chan個post係咪笑我？MSTR同SpaceX兩個portfolio？學生都知我冇錢買SpaceX pre-IPO啦🙏 但BTC/$MSTR方向我認同，明年真係會唔同
clips.text_en_b1: Sailor Moon. You did remember to build a 50/50 MSTR and SpaceX portfolio, right, Anon? Yeah I know SpaceX is private and not every retail guy can buy it, but the point stays. /biz/ keeps pushing this pairing as the real 2026 play, and MSTR is the closest proxy I can actually buy with my prop firm account.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ joke post on MSTR + SpaceX portfolio

signal.rationale: Implied bullish on the MSTR/SpaceX beta as the 2026 trade, MSTR is the only piece retail can actually buy

clips.text_en_b2: Ha, that 4chan post was clearly poking fun at me. Pairing MSTR with SpaceX sounds great in theory, but even a student knows retail traders cannot access SpaceX pre-IPO through any normal channel. That said, I do agree with the broader BTC and MSTR thesis, and 2026 is shaping up very differently from this year. The real question is whether MSTR alone is enough to ride that wave.
clips.text_en_c1: Sailor Moon here, presumably mocking the retail crowd, but the underlying thesis warrants serious consideration. While acquiring pre-IPO SpaceX shares remains firmly outside the reach of most individual investors, MSTR serves as the closest publicly traded proxy, and pairing the two has become something of a mantra on /biz/. My prop firm account permits MSTR exposure with reasonable leverage, which SpaceX simply does not. Provided Bitcoin's trajectory holds, 2026 could indeed look fundamentally different for those positioned accordingly.
clips.text_en_c2: Whether or not /biz/ intended the original post as parody, the broader thesis concerning MSTR's growth and SpaceX's prospective IPO remains, I suspect, fundamentally sound, however aspirational the pairing may appear to a student of markets. Few can plausibly access pre-IPO SpaceX equity, yet as a directional proxy the MSTR-vehicle offers an accessible means of capturing Bitcoin-adjacent upside, particularly within the constraints imposed by a proprietary firm's permitted instruments. The thesis advanced for the coming year, namely that BTC and MSTR will materially decouple from their erstwhile correlation, is, I concede, plausible. Whether the convergence materialises in 2026 is, however, an altogether more speculative matter.

clips.text_zh: 做過深基坑同soil nailing先知，raft foundation幾千噸鋼筋，load path由柱傳落piling cap再傳入岩石。香港IFC兩期都係呢種玩法，美國Skyscraper都係
clips.text_en_b1: I have worked on a few deep foundation jobs in HK with soil nailing and raft slabs for tower blocks. The load path is brutal: every column drops into a pile cap, the pile cap transfers the load to the bored piles, and the piles go down to rock. A single raft for a skyscraper can take thousands of tonnes of rebar.
clips.source_hint: /g/ general tech thread, repurposed for engineering reflection

signal.rationale: Civil engineering reflection, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Having worked on deep excavation and soil nailing projects in Hong Kong, I can tell you the load path in a raft foundation is no joke. Every column channels its load down into a pile cap, which then transfers it through bored piles all the way to bedrock. A single skyscraper raft can swallow thousands of tonnes of rebar. Both phases of IFC followed exactly that approach, and so do most American high-rises.
clips.text_en_c1: Having overseen several deep foundation projects in Hong Kong, I can confirm that the load path is anything but forgiving. Each column channels its tributary load into a pile cap, which subsequently distributes the combined reaction into bored piles terminating in competent bedrock. A single raft beneath a high-rise routinely consumes several thousand tonnes of reinforcing steel. This same structural logic underpinned the IFC Phase 1 and 2 developments, and indeed any supertall constructed in similar geological conditions across the United States.
clips.text_en_c2: Having spent several years engaged upon deep excavation works in Hong Kong, employing soil-nailing techniques and reinforced raft slabs for high-rise construction, one becomes acutely cognisant of the sheer engineering brutality underpinning the load path. Each column transfers its accumulated dead and live loading into a pile cap, the cap in turn redistributes that load across multiple bored piles, and those piles terminate, ultimately, in competent bedrock. A monolithic raft beneath a single skyscraper may consume thousands of tonnes of reinforcing steel. Identical principles governed the construction of IFC Phase 1 and 2, whose architects confronted precisely these geotechnical exigencies.

clips.text_zh: 斜坡survey最尾一定計factor of safety，1.3以下就要加固。香港舊斜坡好多都係1.0-1.2，落大雨就高危。so soil nailing同drainage係基本
clips.text_en_b1: On slope investigation jobs the last thing we always check is the factor of safety. If the calculated FoS drops below about 1.3 the slope needs reinforcement, usually soil nailing plus drainage. A lot of old HK slopes sit around 1.0 to 1.2 on paper, and after a heavy typhoon that is the range where failures start.
clips.source_hint: /g/ generic thread, repurposed for slope FoS talk
clips.text_en_b2: On any slope investigation, the factor of safety is always the final number we check before signing off. If the calculated FoS slips below roughly 1.3, reinforcement is non-negotiable, typically soil nailing combined with proper drainage. Plenty of older Hong Kong slopes sit between 1.0 and 1.2 on paper, which becomes genuinely dangerous once a heavy typhoon rolls through. Those two interventions are really the bare minimum.
clips.text_en_c1: On any slope investigation assignment, the final deliverable invariably hinges on the calculated factor of safety. Should the FoS fall beneath approximately 1.3, remedial intervention becomes mandatory, typically in the form of soil nailing combined with subsurface drainage. Numerous legacy Hong Kong slopes register between 1.0 and 1.2 on paper, a margin that, once saturated during a severe typhoon, places them squarely within the failure envelope. Engineers familiar with the territory will recognise this pattern all too readily.
clips.text_en_c2: Upon the conclusion of any slope investigation, the final calculation invariably concerns the factor of safety, that dimensionless ratio which, when it falls below the prescribed threshold of approximately 1.3, triggers a suite of remediation measures. Soil nailing combined with subsurface drainage constitutes the standard remedial response, since legacy slopes throughout Hong Kong frequently exhibit calculated factors of safety ranging between 1.0 and 1.2. Following sustained typhoon rainfall, such margins become acutely precarious; indeed, this is the precise interval within which slope failures historically initiate, underscoring the importance of vigilant geotechnical assessment.

clips.text_zh: Lab bio佬都開始驚AI，但我哋做site又畫report嘅人仲危險。一張斜坡report AI兩秒出晒，factor of safety、soil nail length都砌到，反不如FE license先保命
clips.text_en_b1: >be me, molecular biofag >notice AI has leapfrogged in just 4 years I do not fear for my job yet like coders do. Labwork needs robotics and biology is messy. But where do you see AI in 5 or 10 years? On a slope report AI can already draft the FoS table and suggest soil nail lengths in seconds, so even site engineers should watch…
clips.source_hint: /g/ anon worried about AI taking lab work

signal.rationale: AI job market worry, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Even lab biology bros are starting to sweat over AI, but honestly the people drafting site reports and drawings are far more exposed. A slope report that used to take a junior engineer days can now be knocked out in seconds, complete with factor of safety tables and suggested soil nail lengths. Robotics still struggles with messy wet-lab work, so I would rather chase a proper FE licence while I still can.
clips.text_en_c1: Even laboratory biologists are beginning to voice unease, yet the white-collar cohort drafting technical documentation faces arguably greater exposure. While wet-lab work demands sophisticated robotics and remains stubbornly resistant to automation, a competent model can already populate an entire slope report, factor-of-safety tables included, within seconds, and propose soil nail lengths that would previously have required hours of manual calculation. Securing a professional engineering licence may prove the only durable hedge against obsolescence.
clips.text_en_c2: While laboratory biologists have begun contemplating their own obsolescence, those of us engaged in site work and report authorship arguably occupy a yet more exposed position. The pace of artificial intelligence's incursion into engineering documentation has been, in the space of mere months, genuinely disquieting. A preliminary slope report, including its factor-of-safety tabulation and preliminary soil-nail length recommendations, can now be drafted in seconds. Consequently, even chartered professionals ought to regard the automation of report-writing with measured apprehension, lest the foundational competencies upon which our licensure rests become commoditised beyond recognition.

clips.text_zh: 中國EV裝sensor影軍演？唔奇啦，香港滿街比亞迪、領克都係咁。中國data back to Beijing係常識，最諷刺係Tesla自己X都有sensor被人講😂
clips.text_en_b1: HAPPENING: Norway catches China EVs spying on military exercises. During a drill to secure Oslo Airport, soldiers found Chinese-owned rental cars had stored videos of them, plus the codes they used to open military gates, and tried to send everything back to China over cellular radio. What does China want with Norway? Will Europe send another sternly worded letter?
clips.text_en_b2: Hardly surprising that Chinese EVs were caught filming military drills, given how saturated Hong Kong streets are with BYDs and Lynk and Co rentals. Everyone already knows Chinese data tends to flow straight back to Beijing, so the Norway story is just the first public confirmation. The real irony is that Tesla cabins are packed with cameras too, yet nobody seems to lose sleep over that.
clips.text_en_c1: Hardly surprising, given how saturated Hong Kong's streets are with BYD and Lynk vehicles of equivalent provenance. The notion that Chinese-manufactured EVs transmit telemetry back to Beijing has long passed into the realm of common knowledge. What renders the situation genuinely absurd is that Tesla, whose own vehicles bristle with sensors of comparable sophistication, has itself attracted scrutiny. Hypocrisy, it seems, cuts in every direction, and consumer privacy remains the perennial casualty of the EV arms race.
clips.text_en_c2: Norwegian forces conducting a recent drill to secure Oslo Airport have reportedly identified rental cars of Chinese provenance surreptitiously recording both the soldiers' movements and the access codes employed at military installations. The vehicles then attempted, via cellular transmission, to relay this footage back to mainland servers. Such conduct ought not to occasion astonishment; Hong Kong's streets teem with BYDs and Lynk & Co vehicles of identical pedigree, whose telemetry is presumed by most analysts to flow routinely back to Beijing. The irony, of course, is that Tesla's own vehicles have attracted comparable accusations—a symmetry devoutly to be noted.

clips.text_zh: 3個post lift死gag，肥仔信笑我「吓你gym咁多年都未溝到女？」btw我都係咁💀 Money first，5年後返美國先諗依樣嘢
clips.text_en_b1: Lost 100 lbs, still no gf. Never had a gf and used to be fat as fuck, about 275 lbs. Started the gym because my sister made her husband take me along. He told me lose the weight and you will find a girl fast. 2.5 years later I am 179 lbs and look pretty fit, but still no gf.
clips.text_en_b2: Dropped roughly 100 pounds after starting the gym on a whim, yet somehow still no girlfriend at 179 pounds and a reasonably fit build. My brother-in-law swore losing the weight would make dating effortless, and two and a half years in I am starting to wonder if he oversold it. Women at the new job do treat me noticeably better, although that might just be the role. Did I grind for nothing, or am I simply being impatient?
clips.text_en_c1: Three posts deep into lifting humour and the fatty crowd still lines up to jeer: surely years in the gym ought to have yielded at least one relationship by now? Fair point, and the honest answer remains no. I shed the weight, held the discipline, redirected every spare dollar into savings rather than nights out. Women at the new workplace treat me noticeably better, though whether that reflects genuine attraction or merely collegial warmth I cannot yet determine.
clips.text_en_c2: After three successive posts eliciting the customary derisive commentary, a gym acquaintance has helpfully observed that, despite my years of dedicated training, romantic success has remained conspicuously absent. His implication, that physical transformation ought to have yielded commensurate relational dividends, is one I can neither confirm nor, frankly, deny. Having once tipped the scales at approximately 275 pounds, and now maintaining a lean 170, the transformation is, by any objective measure, substantial. Yet women at work, who demonstrably treat me with greater cordiality, may simply be responding to a novel professional environment. Patience, perhaps, is the operative virtue.

clips.text_en_c1: The Fall 2026 schedule has been released, and frankly the season looks unremarkable relative to its predecessor. clips.text_en_c2: The forthcoming autumn 2026 anime slate has, by general consensus, proven a disappointingly tepid affair relative to its predecessor. Re:Zero's concluding arc and the latest Demon Slayer instalment represent, in my estimation, the season's sole redeeming features; beyond these, the programming feels predominantly ornamental. Whether this mediocrity reflects scheduling contingencies or a genuine creative drought remains a matter of conjecture. Consolation, however, is to be found in the subsequent summer 2027 offering, notably Nue's Exorcist from Studio Hibari, with Seko's scripting promises sufficient inducement to endure the intervening months of anaemic animation.
